title: Incentives start, identity sustains
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What kept you going at a habit after the first reason ran out?

A student said: I like the instant against delayed gratification. Jose said that the author brushes past statements with deep repercussions, so you have to take notes and ask what your commitment to the idea is.

Jose read a statement from the book: incentives can start a habit, but identity sustains a habit. He said it is a heavy statement: if you see yourself as someone who is in shape and a leader, everything you do reflects that identity.
Jose said that the ending of an experience is vital because we tend to remember it more, so you want the ending of your habit to be satisfying. He asked what the negative side of that is.
A student said: in the short term it is not always pleasurable. When you are working out it is hard, but the long term is that you get in better shape.
Jose said that negative habits stick to us like burrs on our trousers because we look for the immediate reward. He said that when it is going against your identity, you move away from who you are.
A student said: realign the frame so that the habit aligns with your goal. If your biggest goal is to be a leader, reframe working out as a reason people will follow you.
What is the identity behind the habit you are trying to keep?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a habit you started for an incentive.
Write the identity that would keep it going.
Write how the habit ends so it feels satisfying.
Write a short-term cost you accept for a long-term gain.
Write the reframe that links it to your biggest goal.

check.q: What does the book say sustains a habit, as Jose read it?
What did Jose say the ending of an experience is?
choices: Vital because we remember it more

check.q: What did a student say to do with the frame?

recap: Incentives start the habit. Identity keeps it. End it well.
